# p187 — Monitoring Russian and Polish army traffic

**Reading layers:** [Raw output · Edited output · Readable German · Conditional interpretation](../docs/reading-conventions.md). In decoded streams, `?` marks one unresolved position; `X` and numeral/letter labels remain literal.

[Case index](README.md) · [ADFGVX Cipher](../README.md)

**Status:** Earlier joint key recovery verified; incomplete substitution square and residual garbles preserved. **Key:** `CHI-Nov13`.

**Earliest credited record:** [George Lasry, 2017-05-03, comment 50](https://scienceblogs.de/klausis-krypto-kolumne/2017/02/23/the-top-50-unsolved-encrypted-messages-46-unsolved-adfgvx-cryptograms-from-world-war-1/?all=1#comment-878059). **Current source and arithmetic review:** icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro, 2 November 2026.

Norbert proposed the shared-key attack in comment 49; George Lasry recovered the key in comment 50; Norbert refined the labels in comment 53.

## Most likely reading

**Readable German — earlier credited word normalization:**

> [Russischen] und poln. Heeresverkehr voll erfassen. Wichtiges, besonders aus poln. Verkehr, ueber O.H.L.-Station verziffert funken.

**Meaning:** Monitor Russian and Polish army communications in full. Radio important material, especially from Polish traffic, in encrypted form via the Supreme Army Command station.

**Notes:** `poln.` means Polish; `O.H.L.` refers to Supreme Army Command. The source-derived first word ends in `T`, so `RUSSISCHEN` is Norbert's one-letter editorial normalization. The rest of this presentation supplies word divisions and punctuation. The order continues in [p187b](p187b.md).

## Recomputed reading

Variant `audited_CHI_direct`: No received-coordinate edits; only directly attested substitution cells are used.

**Raw output — recomputed direct CHI reading; attested cells only:**

```text
RUSSISCHETUNDPOLNHEERESVERKEHRVOLLERFASSENXWICHTIGESBESONDERSAUSPOLNVERKEHRUEBEROHLSTATIONVERZIFFERTFUNKEN
```

## Review

- Norbert first proposed the shared-key attack in comment 49 on 2017-04-30; George Lasry recovered the key in comment 50 on 2017-05-03; Norbert refined symbol labels in comment 53 the same day.
- The two received texts contain 354 coordinates, 177 plaintext slots. The initial combined publication has 173 letters and incorrectly describes 356 coordinates; four ending slots are not covered by that published string.
- Fourteen square cells remain unassigned. In particular j/x labels were suggested to be digits, not proved to be 0/01.

## Earlier published readings

**Initial substitution labels — [George Lasry, 2017-05-03, comment 50](https://scienceblogs.de/klausis-krypto-kolumne/2017/02/23/the-top-50-unsolved-encrypted-messages-46-unsolved-adfgvx-cryptograms-from-world-war-1/?all=1#comment-878059).**

**Earlier attributed reading:**

```text
RUSSISCHETUNDPOLNHEERESVERGEHRVOLLERFASSENKWICHTIMESBESONDERSAUSPOLNVERGEHRUEBEROHLSTATIONVERZIFFERTFUNGEN
```

**Refined partial substitution labels — [Norbert, 2017-05-03, comment 53](https://scienceblogs.de/klausis-krypto-kolumne/2017/02/23/the-top-50-unsolved-encrypted-messages-46-unsolved-adfgvx-cryptograms-from-world-war-1/?all=1#comment-878079).**

Same text as the recomputed reading above.

**Editorial normalization — [Norbert, 2017-05-03, comment 53](https://scienceblogs.de/klausis-krypto-kolumne/2017/02/23/the-top-50-unsolved-encrypted-messages-46-unsolved-adfgvx-cryptograms-from-world-war-1/?all=1#comment-878079).**

**Earlier attributed reading:**

```text
RUSSISCHENUNDPOLNHEERESVERKEHRVOLLERFASSENXWICHTIGESBESONDERSAUSPOLNVERKEHRUEBEROHLSTATIONVERZIFFERTFUNKEN
```

Conflicts at 1 plaintext positions under the compared variant.

## Verified variants

| Variant | Fixed / total positions | Unpaired suffix | Ordinary re-encryption |
|---|---:|---|---|
| `audited_CHI_direct` | 106 / 106 | — | Yes |

Source strings, edit positions, plaintext domains and attribution are retained in [the prior-reading certificate](../data/prior_readings.json). Re-encryption checks the stated reconstruction, including any conjectural repairs.

# Caucasus hide purchasing — Meierkort, the contract and the Kiew instruction

**Reading layers:** [Raw output · Edited output · Readable German · Conditional interpretation](../../docs/reading-conventions.md). In decoded streams, `?` marks one unresolved position; `X` and numeral/letter labels remain literal.

[All cases](../README.md) · [ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md)

**Source edition and review: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.** Three numbered
parts on pp. 75–76 instruct that hide purchasing is assigned exclusively to
`MEIERKORT`, ask for a signed contract to be returned, keep purchases running
while expenses are settled later, and direct the person in the `WOLTERS`
field to report in Kiew. The names are literal source readings; this edition
does not independently identify the firm or the person's full name.

All three parts repeat the Berlin KRA reference `1521 28/10`, address the
Caucasus representative of the War Ministry, and carry the same reception
time. The typed frames have 836 slots and fix 417 of 418 raw plaintext
positions. Their edited readings need six observed-coordinate substitutions
and one printed-dash fill. An additional 20-slot handwritten annotation on
p76 is preserved as a separate source layer below.

## p75 B1

**Exclusive purchasing and return of the contract.**

[Source crop](../../experiments/late_october_radio_and_materials/sources/p75_B1.png). `B) FUER COS (5.55 a.m., October 29th)` | `BERLIN KRA 1521 28/10 FUER BEVOLLMAECHTIGTER KM KAUKASUS` | `3 TEILE` | `1 TL RICHI-394`.

The typed frame has **394 slots** and fixes **197 of 197 raw plaintext positions** under the unchanged published key.

**Raw output — typed source frame; no word repairs.**

```text
ERSUCHENFIRMAXMEIERKORTXMITZUTEILENDASSEINKAUFVONFELLENIHRALLEINUEBERTRAGENWORDENISTXXFHRMAWAEREZUVERANLASZENDEPIHRVOMHAEUTEEINFUHRSYNDIKATUEBERMITTELTENVERTRAGUNTERSCHRIEBENBALDIGSTZURUECKZUHENDEN
```

**Edited output — only the coordinate changes recorded below.**

```text
ERSUCHENFIRMAXMEIERKORTXMITZUTEILENDASSEINKAUFVONFELLENIHRALLEINUEBERTRAGENWORDENISTXXFIRMAWAEREZUVERANLASSENDENIHRVOMHAEUTEEINFUHRSYNDIKATUEBERMITTELTENVERTRAGUNTERSCHRIEBENBALDIGSTZURUECKZUSENDEN
```

**Readable German — with the five individually priced word repairs:**

> Ersuchen Firma Meierkort mitzuteilen, dass Einkauf von Fellen ihr allein uebertragen worden ist. Firma waere zu veranlassen, den ihr vom Haeute-Einfuhrsyndikat uebermittelten Vertrag unterschrieben baldigst zurueckzusenden.

The instruction assigns the purchase of hides exclusively to the firm and
asks that it return the contract, signed, promptly. `MEIERKORT` and
`HAEUTEEINFUHRSYNDIKAT` are already literal raw labels. The five observed-
coordinate changes repair `FHRMA`, `VERANLASZEN`, `DEP` and
`ZURUECKZUHENDEN`; two coordinates are needed for `VERANLASZEN` → `VERANLASSEN`.

| Typed source index, zero based | Printed | Proposed | Plaintext effect |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 31 | `A` | `D` | Position 87: `H` → `I` |
| 55 | `X` | `V` | Position 106: `Z` → `S` |
| 153 | `A` | `V` | Position 191: `H` → `S` |
| 208 | `V` | `A` | Position 106: `Z` → `S` |
| 297 | `G` | `X` | Position 111: `P` → `N` |

The total is **5 observed-coordinate substitutions and 0 printed-dash fills**. No key cell or rank changes.

## p75 B2

**Expenses later; purchasing must continue.**

[Source crop](../../experiments/late_october_radio_and_materials/sources/p75_B2.png). `Continuation of p75 B, BERLIN KRA 1521 28/10` | `2 TL RICHI-204`.

The typed frame has **204 slots** and fixes **102 of 102 raw plaintext positions** under the unchanged published key.

**Raw output — typed source frame; no word repairs.**

```text
ETWAIGEWUENSCHEBEZUEGLICHSPESENZUSCHUSSWERDENSPAETERGEREGELTWERDENXXEINKAUFDARFNICHTUNTERBROCHENWERDEN
```

**Readable German — spacing and punctuation only:**

> Etwaige Wuensche bezueglich Spesenzuschuss werden spaeter geregelt werden. Einkauf darf nicht unterbrochen werden.

Requests concerning an allowance toward expenses will be settled later;
purchasing is not to be interrupted. This complete 204-coordinate part
requires no repair.

No observed-coordinate substitutions or erased-coordinate fills are needed.

## p76 A3

**Report to Lederzentrale Magnus in Kiew.**

[Source crop](../../experiments/late_october_radio_and_materials/sources/p76_A3.png). `A) FUER COS (5.55 a.m., October 29th)` | `BERLIN KRA 1521 28/10 FUER BEVOLLMAECHTIGTER KM KAUKASUS` | `3 TEILE` | `3 TL RICHI-238`.

The typed frame has **238 slots** and fixes **118 of 119 raw plaintext positions** under the unchanged published key.

### Typed text and handwritten annotation

The [detail image](../../experiments/late_october_radio_and_materials/sources/p76_A3_annotation_detail.png)
contains **238 typed slots**, including one printed dash, and **20 additional
handwritten slots**. After the typed group `FDADA`, handwriting supplies
`FXXFF FDGAD DDDDF AVVFA`; the next four typed groups repeat that sequence.
The working reading uses the 238-slot typed layer, whose length independently
matches `RICHI-238`.

The central handwritten glyph in `DDDDF`, composite source index **87**, is
rounded enough to support **D or O**. `D` is the primary transcription, and
the following typed `DDDDF` supports the duplicate-annotation interpretation;
it does not independently settle that handwritten shape. The alternative
noncoordinate `O` is preserved as a masked diagnostic. Neither reading affects
the typed-only plaintext or its repair ledger.

This layer separation is explicit. If all 258 composite slots are instead
treated as transmitted material, obtaining the typed-only frame requires
excluding **20 slots**, containing **20 observed coordinates under D** or
**19 observed coordinates and one noncoordinate mask under O**. That is a
separate conditional model, not a zero-cost deletion of transmitted symbols.
The certificate retains both composite decodes and their full position maps.

**Raw output — typed source frame; no word repairs.**

```text
ANWESENHEITWOLTERSNICHTMEHRERFORDERLICHERSUCHENIHNANZUWEISENNACHKIEWABZUREISENUNDSICH3ORTBEILEDERZENTRALEMAGNUSZU?ELDEN
```

**Edited output — only the coordinate changes recorded below.**

```text
ANWESENHEITWOLTERSNICHTMEHRERFORDERLICHERSUCHENIHNANZUWEISENNACHKIEWABZUREISENUNDSICHDORTBEILEDERZENTRALEMAGNUSZUMELDEN
```

**Readable German — under the typed-only source layer:**

> Anwesenheit Wolters nicht mehr erforderlich. Ersuchen ihn anzuweisen, nach Kiew abzureisen und sich dort bei Lederzentrale Magnus zu melden.

The person's presence is no longer required; the instruction is to leave for
Kiew and report to `LEDERZENTRALE MAGNUS`. The field `WOLTERS` is kept as
printed by decryption; this does not decide whether its final `S` is part of
the surname or a grammatical ending. The raw `3ORT` becomes `DORT` through
one observed-coordinate substitution. The printed dash supplies the `M` in
`MELDEN`; the full unchanged-key domain before the fill is `TGLMVN`.

| Typed source index, zero based | Printed | Proposed | Plaintext effect |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 101 | `F` | `V` | Position 85: `3` → `D` |

There are **1 printed-dash fills**, listed individually with their original row, group, source index and plaintext effect in the certificate. The total is **1 observed-coordinate substitutions and 1 printed-dash fills**. No key cell or rank changes.

The source prints the following **cleartext signature**, outside the
ciphertext frame:

```text
KRIEGSAMT KRIEGSROHSTOFF
ABTEILUNG RR L 506/10 KRA
```

It is a source transcription, not additional decoded plaintext. The date and
reference are retained literally.

## Evidence, verification and credit

The [literal inputs](../../experiments/late_october_radio_and_materials/inputs.json),
[coordinate certificates](../../experiments/late_october_radio_and_materials/certificates.json)
and [source images](../../experiments/late_october_radio_and_materials/README.md)
preserve the complete source, unchanged published key, raw outputs and every
proposed repair. The source is J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX
Cipher System*, printed pp. 74–76 / PDF pp. 77–79. Its page heading is
28 October 1918; the printed reception times include 29 October and are not
silently reconciled.

The October 28–31 key is prior work credited to George Lasry and colleagues.
The [prior-evidence snapshot](../../experiments/late_october_radio_and_materials/prior_evidence.json)
retains the earlier unreviewed repository OCR candidates, including mostly
readable p74 A/B and p75 A3. The present contribution is the source edition,
additional complete bodies, explicit source-layer separation and reproducible
repair ledger by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**. No first-historical-
decipherment priority is claimed.

```sh
python3 experiments/late_october_radio_and_materials/verify.py --verify
python3 experiments/late_october_radio_and_materials/verify.py --verify --pdf /path/to/childs.pdf
```

# Late October radio service — calls, garbled traffic and network routing

**Reading layers:** [Raw output · Edited output · Readable German · Conditional interpretation](../../docs/reading-conventions.md). In decoded streams, `?` marks one unresolved position; `X` and numeral/letter labels remain literal.

[All cases](../README.md) · [ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md)

**Source edition and review: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.** Five physical
records on pp. 74–75 describe daily calls, a garbled CHI telegram, and questions
about message routing between radio stations and the German wire network.
The five typed frames contain 756 slots. Their unchanged-key outputs fix
348 of 378 plaintext positions. The proposed readings use five observed-
coordinate substitutions and 30 printed-dash fills; all 30 fills belong to
p74 C1 and remain an explicitly conditional reconstruction.

The three routing parts are printed as p74 C1/C2 and p75 A3. The change of
section letter is retained. The repeated recipient line, `1900 (28.10)`,
`3 TEILE`, numbered parts and page continuation support treating them as one
three-part source sequence.

## p74 A

**Daily calls from Deutsch-Altenburg.**

[Source crop](../../experiments/late_october_radio_and_materials/sources/p74_A.png). `A) OSM, NKJ, COS v LP (3.50 p.m., October 28th)` | `1630` | `RIZI-154`.

The typed frame has **154 slots** and fixes **77 of 77 raw plaintext positions** under the unchanged published key.

**Raw output — typed source frame; no word repairs.**

```text
DEUTSIHALTENBURGXOHDXWIRDSIEVOMX29XABTAEGLICHUMX1120XMXEXZXWELLEX5200XANRUFEN
```

**Edited output — only the coordinate changes recorded below.**

```text
DEUTSCHALTENBURGXOHDXWIRDSIEVOMX29XABTAEGLICHUMX1120XMXEXZXWELLEX5200XANRUFEN
```

**Readable German — with the one recorded word repair:**

> Deutsch-Altenburg, OHD, wird Sie vom 29. ab taeglich um 11:20 M. E. Z., Welle 5200, anrufen.

The printed source has `RIZI-154`. The repair changes `DEUTSIH` to
`DEUTSCH`; it does not assign the station code or any numeral. The time colon,
hyphen and punctuation are display formatting. `OHD`, `29`, `1120` and `5200`
are unchanged literal labels under the published full square. The ciphertext
does not print a wavelength unit, so this edition does not add one.

| Typed source index, zero based | Printed | Proposed | Plaintext effect |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 85 | `A` | `G` | Position 5: `I` → `C` |

The total is **1 observed-coordinate substitutions and 0 printed-dash fills**. No key cell or rank changes.

## p74 B

**Repeat the garbled parts of a CHI telegram.**

[Source crop](../../experiments/late_october_radio_and_materials/sources/p74_B.png). `B) NKJ v LP (6.10 a.m., October 29th)` | `FUER COS 2200 (28.10)` | `RICHI-170`.

The typed frame has **170 slots** and fixes **85 of 85 raw plaintext positions** under the unchanged published key.

**Raw output — typed source frame; no word repairs.**

```text
KAUKASUSDELEGAXSPRUCHTLGRLEITSTX639XOSKACHIX212GR3TLVERSTX2U3TLWHXNACHCHEFRM5X15031UX
```

**Readable German — abbreviations retained or explicitly expanded:**

> Kaukasus-Delega[tion]: Spruch Tlgr.-Leitst. 639, OSKA, CHI, 212 Gr., 3 Tl., verst[ümmelt]. 2 u[nd] 3 Tl. w[ieder]h[olen]. Nach[richten]chef RM 5, 15031 U.

The brackets are proposed expansions of telegram shorthand, not supplied
ciphertext. The message refers to a three-part CHI telegram as garbled and
requests repetition of its second and third parts. `OSKA` and the reference
fields remain unexpanded. The word `CHI` belongs to the decoded report;
this physical record is headed `RICHI-170` and uses the ordinary period key.

No observed-coordinate substitutions or erased-coordinate fills are needed.

## p74 C1

**First routing part with six erased groups.**

[Source crop](../../experiments/late_october_radio_and_materials/sources/p74_C1.png). `C) FUER CVS, TAGANROG, POT (ASO) v LP (6.15 a.m., October 29th)` | `1900 (28.10) 3 TEILE` | `1 TL RICHI-148`.

The typed frame has **148 slots** and fixes **44 of 74 raw plaintext positions** under the unchanged published key.

**Raw output — typed source frame; no word repairs.**

```text
ZUR?G???FTVE?K???SHAN?E???CHIF?E???EIST?T???LLEA?D???SCHESD???NETZAG???HLX
```

**Edited output — conditional supplied reading of the printed erasures.**

```text
ZUREGELNFTVERKEHRSHANDELSSCHIFFEXWIEISTFTSTELLEANDEUTSCHESDRHTNETZAGESCHLX
```

**Conditional interpretation:** The source begins with six printed
five-dash groups, exactly 30 erased coordinate slots. The full edited string
is one ordinary-language fill candidate consistent with every observed
coordinate. The 44 fixed raw labels and all partial-cell domains are preserved
in the certificate. This is not a uniqueness result for the missing wording.

The candidate opening `ZUREGELNFTVERKEHRSHANDELSSCHIFFE` is retained literally.
This edition does not choose a grammatical expansion for its `S` or silently
rewrite the phrase. The following readable excerpt begins at the next
sentence; only that already displayed opening is omitted from the excerpt.

**Readable German — excerpt of the conditional fill candidate:**

> Wie ist FT-Stelle an deutsches Dr[a]htnetz a[n]geschl[ossen]?

The bracketed letters are prose expansions of the edited abbreviations
`DRHTNETZ` and `AGESCHL`; they do not add decoded positions. The question asks
how the FT station is connected to the German wire network. Its appearance
inside the three-part routing sequence supports this reading, but does not
turn the 30 missing source coordinates into observations.

There are **30 printed-dash fills**, listed individually with their original row, group, source index and plaintext effect in the certificate. The total is **0 observed-coordinate substitutions and 30 printed-dash fills**. No key cell or rank changes.

## p74 C2

**Lines used to exchange foreign-station telegrams.**

[Source crop](../../experiments/late_october_radio_and_materials/sources/p74_C2.png). `Continuation of p74 C, 1900 (28.10) 3 TEILE` | `2 TL RICHI-130`.

The typed frame has **130 slots** and fixes **65 of 65 raw plaintext positions** under the unchanged published key.

**Raw output — typed source frame; no word repairs.**

```text
AUFWELCHENLTGNERFLGTAUSTAUSCH5ERTELGRMHTFREMDLAENDSCHENSTATIONENX
```

**Edited output — only the coordinate changes recorded below.**

```text
AUFWELCHENLTGNERFLGTAUSTAUSCHDERTELGRMITFREMDLAENDSCHENSTATIONENX
```

**Readable German — with the two priced repairs and marked expansions:**

> Auf welchen Ltgn [Leitungen] erf[o]lgt Austausch der Telgr. [Telegramme] mit fremdlaend[i]schen Stationen?

The bracketed full words expand the literal abbreviations `LTGN` and
`TELGR`; `[o]` and `[i]` are prose spelling completions of `ERFLGT` and
`FREMDLAENDSCHEN`. They are not extra decoded letters. The two coordinate
repairs instead change raw `5ER` to `DER` and raw `MHT` to `MIT`.
The raw numeral label `5` is retained in the raw block and is priced as a
word repair; no numerical field or key-square digit is reassigned.

| Typed source index, zero based | Printed | Proposed | Plaintext effect |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 46 | `D` | `V` | Position 29: `5` → `D` |
| 47 | `A` | `D` | Position 38: `H` → `I` |

The total is **2 observed-coordinate substitutions and 0 printed-dash fills**. No key cell or rank changes.

## p75 A3

**Via the German station or a separate line.**

[Source crop](../../experiments/late_october_radio_and_materials/sources/p75_A3.png). `A) FUER CVS, TAGANROG, POT (ASO) v LP (6.15 a.m., October 29th)` | `1900 (28.10) 3 TEILE` | `3 TL RICHI-154`.

The typed frame has **154 slots** and fixes **77 of 77 raw plaintext positions** under the unchanged published key.

**Raw output — typed source frame; no word repairs.**

```text
DURCHVERMITTLGDERDEUTSSCHENSTATIONOZUEAERRBESONDLTGNUWOHINXNACHCHEF3AX110701X
```

**Edited output — only the coordinate changes recorded below.**

```text
DURCHVERMITTLGDERDEUTSSCHENSTATIONODUEBERRBESONDLTGNUWOHINXNACHCHEF3AX110701X
```

**Readable German — spelling peculiarities retained:**

> Durch Vermittlg [Vermittlung] der deutsschen Station od[er] ueberr besond[ere] Ltgn [Leitungen], u[nd] wohin? Nach[richten]chef 3 A, 110701.

The doubled `S` in `DEUTSSCHEN` and doubled `R` in `UEBERR` are present in
both raw and edited streams and are deliberately retained here. The brackets
expand abbreviations only. The message asks whether routing is through the
German station or separate lines, and where those lines lead. The two priced
repairs are `OZ` → `OD` and `UEAERR` → `UEBERR`; the `3A` and `110701` fields
remain unchanged.

| Typed source index, zero based | Printed | Proposed | Plaintext effect |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 55 | `V` | `F` | Position 38: `A` → `B` |
| 72 | `X` | `V` | Position 35: `Z` → `D` |

The total is **2 observed-coordinate substitutions and 0 printed-dash fills**. No key cell or rank changes.

## Evidence, verification and credit

The [literal inputs](../../experiments/late_october_radio_and_materials/inputs.json),
[coordinate certificates](../../experiments/late_october_radio_and_materials/certificates.json)
and [source images](../../experiments/late_october_radio_and_materials/README.md)
preserve the complete source, unchanged published key, raw outputs and every
proposed repair. The source is J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX
Cipher System*, printed pp. 74–76 / PDF pp. 77–79. Its page heading is
28 October 1918; the printed reception times include 29 October and are not
silently reconciled.

The October 28–31 key is prior work credited to George Lasry and colleagues.
The [prior-evidence snapshot](../../experiments/late_october_radio_and_materials/prior_evidence.json)
retains the earlier unreviewed repository OCR candidates, including mostly
readable p74 A/B and p75 A3. The present contribution is the source edition,
additional complete bodies, explicit source-layer separation and reproducible
repair ledger by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**. No first-historical-

# A regimental journey report with unresolved route and unit labels

**Reading layers:** [Raw output · Edited output · Readable German · Conditional interpretation](../../docs/reading-conventions.md). In decoded streams, `?` marks one unresolved position; `X` and numeral/letter labels remain literal.

**Source review and edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

This two-part native report describes a journey and assistance received after minor interruptions. The route, date-like and unit labels remain in their exact source form. The five printed dashes in part 1 are explicit source erasures: four are supplied by priced wording proposals and one remains unresolved. The Nov28–Dec1 square uses Y as the separator; X inside the displayed labels stays literal.

## Source and scope

[Childs source](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view) · [Reviewed p225 excerpt](../../experiments/regimental_journey_report/sources/p225_reviewed.png) · [Inputs](../../experiments/regimental_journey_report/inputs.json) · [Position and change certificates](../../experiments/regimental_journey_report/certificates.json)

The published `Nov28-Dec1` key is unchanged. [Original OCR records](../../experiments/regimental_journey_report/ocr_snapshot.json) and [reproducible comparisons with that earlier evidence](../../experiments/regimental_journey_report/prior_candidates.json) are preserved separately. The present edition supplies checked source framing, exact costs and readable passages; it makes no first-public-decipherment claim.

| Record | Source slots | Fixed raw positions | Observed substitutions | Source-mask fills |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| [p225 B1](#p225-b1) | 254 | 122 / 127 | 8 | 4 |
| [p225 B2](#p225-b2) | 212 | 106 / 106 | 2 | 0 |

## p225 B1

**Source transcription — header:** `B) ZON v UKS (01.17 a.m., November 29th); 1130 (11/28) (VON BSL); 1 TL RICHI-254`

# Alpenkorps departure and march report

**Reading layers:** [Raw output · Edited output · Readable German · Conditional interpretation](../../docs/reading-conventions.md). In decoded streams, `?` marks one unresolved position; `X` and numeral/letter labels remain literal.

A conditional second-part reading concerns preparations to transport the Alpenkorps and the continuation of a march. The source is dated 8 November 1918; the receipt header is 11.44 p.m. on 8 November. The first part of this physical p160 transmission has not been identified. The place-like strings NAGYBESKEREK and WERGCHEEZ are left exactly as decoded.

Source: Childs, printed pp.160–161 (PDF pp.163–164). [Source images and inputs](../../experiments/nov8_radio_keys_and_reports/inputs.json), [certificates](../../experiments/nov8_radio_keys_and_reports/certificates.json), [method and limitations](../../experiments/nov8_radio_keys_and_reports/README.md). All indices below are zero-based.

## p160 A2

Header: `A) UKS v ZON (11.44 p.m., November 8th); 1915 (8/11) 2 TLE; 2 TL; RICHI-238`.

Literal 240 versus advertised 238. The two six-character groups occupy source 15–20 and 26–31; the primary conditional frame excludes 19 and 26. The first part of this physical p160 transmission is not identified. ZON is a separate cleartext footer. WERGCHEEZ and NAGYBESKEREK stay literal.

The source has **240 slots** (239 valid coordinates). The conditional model has 238 slots / 119 plaintext positions: 117 fixed raw, 118 fixed after the stated edits.

**Cost:** 4 observed-coordinate substitutions; 1 printed-mask fill; 2 observed-coordinate exclusions; 0 mask exclusions; no inserted coordinates.

**Raw output** — under the explicitly conditional exclusion frame:

```text
ALPENKOYPSW2RDUJVERBASZZUMABTRFNSPORTBEREIT?ESTELLTXX219X217XUNU?XREXSETZEN9X11XMARSCHINLINIENAGYBESKEREKXWERGCHEEZFORT
```

**Edited output** — changes and source offsets are enumerated in the certificate:

```text
ALPENKORPSWIRDUJVERBASZZUMABTRANSPORTBEREITGESTELLTXX219X217XUND?XREXSETZEN9X11XMARSCHINLINIENAGYBESKEREKXWERGCHEEZFORT
```

**Readable German** — spacing, case, punctuation and conventional umlaut rendering only; all non-`X` labels match the edited output:

> Alpenkorps wird Ujverbasz zum Abtransport bereitgestellt. 219, 217 und ? Re. setzen 9.11 Marsch in Linie Nagybeskerek, Wergcheez fort.

## Parallel traffic and an additional interpretation

The previously reviewed [p170 B1/B2 and p166/p167 reports](nov9_operational_reports.md)
provide related earlier-part context and a near-identical second part. The
source headers differ: this p160 transmission is received on November 8,
while p170 B is received on November 9. The parallel does not identify the
missing physical first part of this particular p160 transmission.

Under the explicitly stated 238-slot p160 exclusion frame, its alignment
with p170 B2 has **230 known-coordinate agreements, six known disagreements
and two complementary masks**. P160 frame25 (literal source27) supplies X
where p170 has a mask, supporting the latter's proposed J in `UJVERBASZ`.
P170 frame183 supplies D where p160 source185 is a dash, supporting the
p160 fill in `BEREITGESTELLT`. These are conditional cross-witness supports;
all six disagreements remain recorded.

**Conditional interpretation:** substituting the parallel's `RD` and
`WERSCHETZ` for the primary `RE` and `WERGCHEEZ` costs **three additional
observed-coordinate substitutions** at p160 source18 D→X, source48 G→X
and source192 D→G. Its total is seven observed substitutions, one printed-mask
fill and two observed exclusions. This separately priced interpretation is
not substituted into the primary edited or readable stream above.

The [parallel certificate](../../experiments/nov8_radio_keys_and_reports/parallel_witnesses.json)
retains every source and plaintext difference, prior record identity and both
complete 5/6 key witnesses. The earlier operational case's historical unit
identification remains a separate context layer; no unknown digit is filled
in this source edition. No previously cataloged parallel is counted again.

## Shared uncertainty and credit

The two missing square cells `VF` and `XA` jointly contain `5` and `6`. Both complete assignments are retained as compatibility witnesses; every occurrence of a cell shares the same digit. The displayed `?` positions therefore must not be treated as independent digit choices. In p160 B2 one additional source coordinate remains unfilled; its domain can include letters as well as digits.

The published Nov7–9 period key and earlier OCR candidates are credited in the inputs. This edition adds source inspection, separate repair costs and exact readable-text mappings. It does not claim new recovery of the period key.

# Mecklenburg inquiry about a letter to Herzog Karl Michael

**Reading layers:** [Raw output · Edited output · Readable German · Conditional interpretation](../../docs/reading-conventions.md). In decoded streams, `?` marks one unresolved position; `X` and numeral/letter labels remain literal.

**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Childs p141 A, PDF p144, contains two parts received under
`ASO v LP (08.12 p.m., November 6th)`, with `FUER ASO (6/11) 2 TLE`.
The Mecklenburg legation requests quick answers through
Kapitänleutnant Wagner and the Tiflis consulate. The second part asks about a
July letter to Herzog Karl Michael and his opportunity to respond. The
wording is awkward in one place and is preserved below.

## p141 A1

The [first-part crop](../../experiments/mecklenburg_and_seaplane_personnel/sources/p141_A1.png)
has **304 slots**, matching `1 TL RICHI-304`. There is one printed dash
and one unreadable visible glyph. The unchanged published **Nov4–6** key
fixes **150 / 152 positions** before editing.

**Raw output — native 304-coordinate frame:**

```text
BXMXKXSEWASTOPOLX?ECKLENBURGISCHEGESZNDTSCHAFTBITTETDRINZENDBEIKAPITAENLEUTNANTXWAGNERXUNDKONSULATXTIFLISXSCHNELLEBEANTWORTUNGFOLGEN?ERFRAGENZUERWIRKENX
```

**Edited output — three observed-coordinate substitutions, one printed-dash fill and one unreadable-glyph fill:**

```text
BXMXKXSEWASTOPOLXMECKLENBURGISCHEGESANDTSCHAFTBITTETDRINGENDBEIKAPITAENLEUTNANTXWAGNERXUNDKONSULATXTIFLISXSCHNELLEBEANTWORTUNGFOLGENDERFRAGENZUERWIRKENX
```

**Readable German — spacing and punctuation:**

> B. M. K., Sewastopol. Mecklenburgische Gesandtschaft bittet dringend,
> bei Kapitänleutnant Wagner und Konsulat Tiflis schnelle Beantwortung
> folgender Fragen zu erwirken.

The `?` inside the ciphertext transcription's group `XAX?F` is a
placeholder for an indeterminate visible mark at source **68**, not a
printed question mark or an omitted source slot. The candidate supplies F,
yielding the D in `FOLGENDER`. The printed dash at source **109** is filled
with X, yielding the M in `MECKLENBURGISCHE`.

## p141 A2

The [second-part crop](../../experiments/mecklenburg_and_seaplane_personnel/sources/p141_A2.png)
contains **422 slots**, including six printed dashes, exactly matching
`2 TL RICHI-422`. Its raw reading fixes **205 / 211 positions**.

**Raw output — native 422-coordinate frame:**

```text
1XST?PXISTBEKANNTXOBDASIMJULIANXHERZOGXKARLXMICHAELXABGESANDTHANDSCHREIBENDESGROSSHERZOGSABGESANDTWOODENISTX2XSTOPXISTBEKANNTXOBHERZOGGE?EGENHWIT?UEINERR?ECKAEUSS?RUNGGEH?BTHATXBESTAETIGUNGXAUMIRALSTABX32982XBX2
```

**Edited output — five observed-coordinate substitutions and six printed-dash fills:**

```text
1XSTOPXISTBEKANNTXOBDASIMJULIANXHERZOGXKARLXMICHAELXABGESANDTHANDSCHREIBENDESGROSSHERZOGSABGESANDTWORDENISTX2XSTOPXISTBEKANNTXOBHERZOGGELEGENHEITZUEINERRUECKAEUSSERUNGGEHABTHATXBESTAETIGUNGXADMIRALSTABX32982XBX2
```

**Readable German — spacing and punctuation; one grammatical spelling expansion is bracketed:**

> 1. Stop. Ist bekannt, ob das im Juli an Herzog Karl Michael
> abgesandt[e] Handschreiben des Grossherzogs abgesandt worden ist?
> 2. Stop. Ist bekannt, ob Herzog Gelegenheit zu einer Rückäusserung
> gehabt hat? Bestätigung. Admiralstab. 32982. B. 2.

The first **ABGESANDT** is directly adjacent to **HANDSCHREIBEN** in the
edited stream. The bracketed E makes that adjective readable in normal
German but is **not** an encoded plaintext position. The later repeated
**ABGESANDT** is also literal. This edition does not silently replace
either occurrence with “delivered,” “received,” or another smoother verb.

## Conditional interpretation and source limits

The primary editions accept a faded G at A1 source **161** and a faint A
at A2 source **279**. The
[detail crop](../../experiments/mecklenburg_and_seaplane_personnel/sources/p141_A1_glyphs.png)
shows the first glyph, and the
[faint group ending](../../experiments/mecklenburg_and_seaplane_personnel/sources/p141_A2_faint_end.png)
shows the second. Their masked alternatives remain in the certificate:

- Masking A1 source161 changes the initial **B** of `BXMXK` to domain
  **8ABGIR**. The variant leaves that code character unresolved.
- Masking A2 source279 changes the **E** of the first `ABGESANDT` to
  domain **9EKVXZ**. That variant also leaves its position unresolved.

Each alternative retains all six exact re-encryption witnesses. No newly
masked glyph is filled simply to preserve the primary reading. The
variants do not add physical records or enter the primary counts.

The names, titles and questions are what the telegram says. This source
edition does not independently identify the grand duke, confirm a letter's
dispatch or reply, or expand the `B.M.K.` address and `32982 B2` reference.
The two primary candidates together contain **363 positions**, use **eight
observed substitutions and eight source fills**, and re-encrypt exactly.
There is no frame or key change.

Both bodies were already partly readable in earlier repository screens.
Their prior credit and the published key are retained. The
[inputs](../../experiments/mecklenburg_and_seaplane_personnel/inputs.json),
[certificates](../../experiments/mecklenburg_and_seaplane_personnel/certificates.json)
and [reproduction instructions](../../experiments/mecklenburg_and_seaplane_personnel/README.md)
provide the complete source and editing ledger.

| [Lasry dissertation](https://www.uni-kassel.de/upress/online/OpenAccess/978-3-7376-0458-1.OpenAccess.pdf) | Independent corroboration of partial key squares. |
| [Bourdeau's review](https://dbourdeau.github.io/cyphersolver/adfgvx.html) | Reviewed status and plaintext-constraint checks; inspected 2 November 2026. |

The included excerpts reproduce the historical US government source pages needed to inspect specific claims. The complete book and modern editorial material are not redistributed. Original German, French, and ciphertext are quoted as research data; repository discussion is in English.

## p152 terminology

`STRUSEN` is a genuine silk-trade term, not an error requiring normalization. [Guérin-Mèneville's 1853 report in the Polytechnisches Journal](https://dingler.bbaw.de/articles/ar128114.html), volume 128, p. 451, identifies it with the outer cocoon layer. This independently supports the commodity context of the raw decipherment.


## Bibliographic distinctions

The Aegean volume's 2000 edition date is supported by Lasry's bibliography; the inspected imprint is undated. Its opening technical paper matches *General Solution for the ADFGVX Cipher System*, Register 129, whose separate government title page states 1934. That publication date is distinct from the date of Childs's wartime records and from the composition date of the earlier manuscript.

*German Military Ciphers from February to November 1918* is a different report, published in 1935 with Friedman's foreword dated 25 June 1934. The foreword dates Childs's underlying report to about December 1918 and identifies later added notes. Exact source identifiers and evidence are in [the registry](registry.json).

## Header direction

`X v Y` means **recipient X, sender Y**. The explicit routes and adjacent headers on [printed p. 9 of the 1935 report](excerpts/nsa_header_convention_p9.png) establish the convention: `NKJ v LP` accompanies a message from LP through NKJ, and `OSM v COS` accompanies a message from COS to OSM. Thus `CM v CZ` is CZ to CM; `-- v CM` has an unknown recipient and a known sender CM. A relay call sign need not identify the ultimate author or addressee.

## Historical and technical context

These sources support specific interpretations or delimit a search. They do not
replace a missing ciphertext witness or assign an unknown key cell.

| Source | Use and limit |
|---|---|
| [Paquet, Groener and Hopman records, edited by Winfried Baumgart in 1971](https://digitale-sammlungen.de/en/details/bsb00042051) | Contemporary shipping and Crimea command context for p155 and the conditional p215 Kosch reading. Diary/document text is distinguished from the modern editor's notes. |
| [Telefunken-Zeitung, 1919, no. 15](https://www.radiomuseum.org/forumdata/users/5100/TZ_3Jg_Nr15_1v1_v10.pdf) | The manufacturer's contemporary terminology supports the undamped-wave radio-apparatus interpretation of `US GERAETE` in the p197/p198 equipment traffic. No particular model is established. |
| [Australian War Memorial, Allied-fleet memorandum of 24 November 1918](https://transcribe.awm.gov.au/transcription/item/rcdig0000179-4) | Independent Black Sea departure-order context for p217. It does not verify p215's reported troops or explain its nationalities. |
| [Kress, *Meine Mission im Kaukasus*, 2001 edition](https://de.scribd.com/document/46043064/General-Der-Artillerie-a-D-Friedrich-Freiherr-Kress-von-Kressenstein-MEINE-MISSION-IM-KAUKASUS) | A retrospective memoir accompanying a 1943 covering letter. The bounded late-period inspection finds no matching p73 radiogram; an apparent calendar-date match belongs to the editor's 1917 discussion. |
| [Lepsius, *Deutschland und Armenien 1914–1918*, 1919](https://www.gutenberg.org/files/58144/58144-h/58144-h.htm) | Documents 439–444 were checked. Document 442 is Kress's outgoing 30 October report, not the sought incoming p73 message. |

Exact page/image locators, inspected scopes and limitations are retained in
[the registry](registry.json) and the linked case and review records. The
[two held-out books](../experiments/open_targets/heldout_sources.json) used for
statistical calibration have separate source and byte-hash provenance; their
prose is not treated as a source for any historical telegram's wording.

# Hungary transport warning: a witnessed missing group

**ADFGVX Cipher — icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**

This edition covers six physical parts on Childs printed p184 (PDF p187): B1–B3 and C1–C3. Two three-part transmissions warn the Mackensen command's mineral-oil department against letting transports from Romania enter Hungary. The source says they would be completely lost there. That is the message's warning, not an independently established outcome.

The useful restoration is **B2's missing five-coordinate group `DXDVA`**. The source advertises 192 coordinates but prints 187. An alignment containing 92 directly readable positions from the uncorrected C2 body singles out gap 35, before the eighth printed group, among all 188 possible placements of one contiguous five-coordinate gap. It restores five plaintext letters with **zero changes to observed B2 coordinates**. The uniqueness claim is conditional on this explicit gap model and alignment.

The [reading edition](../../cases/military/hungary_transport_warning.md) gives all six raw strings, the conservative candidates and the source differences. The principal evidence is [inputs.json](inputs.json), [certificates.json](certificates.json), and the [source crops](sources/).

## What is and is not identical

Both source headers say from LP for UKS, origin `13.40 (13/11)`, three parts. B is received as `NKJ v LP (02.51 a.m., November 13th)` and C as `ZO'N v NKJ (02.15 a.m., November 13th)`. These morning receipts precede the stated origin time on the same printed date. We preserve that inconsistency and do not repair the date or time.

The address parts differ in length and received spelling. B1 has `MACKENSEN`, `MINERALOEL` and `BUCKAREST`; C1 has `MKENSEN`, `MINERALOL` and `BUMAREST`. These differences are not silently normalized.

The body parts also differ. C2 has an extra unresolved position in `HE?REIN`, omits the separator between `RESTLOS` and `VERLOREN`, and ends with one X where B2 ends with two. Two ordinary-letter repairs in C2, `TRANSTORTE → TRANSPORTE` and `TIND → SIND`, are witnessed by unchanged B2 letters. Those two witness positions were excluded from the gap-selection mask, avoiding circular support.

B3 and C3 have exactly the same coordinate pairs for all 54 C3 plaintext positions. B3 adds one terminal X. This exact pair agreement includes 15 unresolved reference positions per copy; it does not supply their labels. The faint C3 groups `AXADX` and `DFVGA` have a separate eight-times-scale crop documenting the literal source reading.

## The missing-group certificate

All indices are zero-based. Five coordinates are absent before source index 35. The screen constructs its masked plaintext **from C2's uncorrected raw text**, using these correspondence ranges:

| B2 start | C2 start | Matching positions |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 0 | 0 | 5 |
| 6 | 6 | 39 |
| 45 | 46 | 35 |
| 81 | 81 | 9 |
| 91 | 91 | 4 |

B2 positions 5, 80, 90 and 95 are excluded. All 188 gap scores are frozen. Gap 35 alone needs zero observed-coordinate substitutions; gaps 34, 36 and 37 each need one. The five missing stencil coordinates are all determined by the mask and equal `DXDVA`.

| Restored B2 plaintext position | Character | Uncorrected C2 witness position |
|---:|:---:|---:|
| 8 | T | 8 |
| 18 | A | 18 |
| 28 | H | 28 |
| 79 | S | 80 |
| 89 | X | 89 |

Full re-encryption of the restored B2 plaintext reproduces every printed coordinate in order and the inserted group. The verifier separately derives the inserted group from the C2 mask, before using the full B2 candidate.

## Counts and limits

The package preserves 877 printed coordinates and models 882 after the five-coordinate gap. There are 441 plaintext positions: 405 fixed under the source-aligned models, 410 after the witnessed fills and two C2 substitutions. Thirty-one positions remain unresolved: 30 footer positions and C2's extra word position.

The last position has received pair `DX`, source indices 90 and 137, and unchanged domain `0123456789QY`. The footer domains are also retained in full. No partial-square cell, digit, rank, address length or date is changed.

Earlier unreviewed repository screens already contained recognizable address, warning and footer material; their relevant candidate records and hashes are frozen. A bounded check of the Lasry–Niebel–Kopal–Wacker paper, Lasry dissertation and cached 2017 discussion found no explicit discussion of this body. This is not proof of historical priority. The contribution is a source edition, a new source-supported missing-group certificate and a fully auditable distinction between exact matches and received differences.

## Reproduce

From the repository root, using Python 3.10 or later:

```sh
python experiments/hungary_transport_warning/verify.py --verify
python experiments/hungary_transport_warning/verify.py --verify --pdf /path/to/adfgvx-childs.pdf
```

The first command uses the standard library and the repository's cipher module. It recomputes the inverse permutation independently, checks every position and domain against the cipher module, reruns all 188 gap models, verifies the complete pairwise footer comparison, and checks the frozen certificate and crop hashes. The optional PDF check additionally requires PyMuPDF and Pillow; it checks the PDF hash and reproduces every crop pixel for pixel.

# Surviving parts of an eight-part Transylvania situation report

Prepared by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**.

This package gives exact source editions for **five readable surviving parts: 1, 4, 5, 7 and 8**. It also preserves the unread fragment of part 6 separately. Parts 2 and 3 have not been located. The assembly is a proposed association of physical sources on Childs pp128, 129 and 137, supported by their matching `1840 / 18.40`, `8 TLE` and `LP v NKJ` fields, their part numbers, the published Nov4–6 key, and coherent military-withdrawal content. The inconsistent page/receipt dates and times remain explicit.

The first source page itself says that parts 2–6 are missing. That statement is accurate for its copy and is preserved in the source crop. A separate page supplies part 4, an interference-damaged part 5 and a short surviving fragment of part 6. These are not invented continuations or an exact duplicated-plaintext witness.

## Source association and conflicting headings

| Physical source | Surviving parts | Page heading | Receipt line | Origin/message fields |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| p128 B | 1 | 5 November | 7.25 p.m., 5 November | `1840 8 TLE` |
| p129 A | 7–8 | 5 November, continued | 7.01 p.m., 5 November | `1840 8 TLE` |
| p137 A | 4–6 | **6 November** | **08.14, 5 November**, no a.m./p.m. qualifier | `18.40 8 TLE VON UKS 18.40` |

All three name `LP v NKJ`. The report's sender is consistent with the raw `OXKXM` signature/content and p137's explicit UKS field. This is evidence for the proposed association, not a solution to the anomalous timing. In particular, p137's 08.14 receipt is not silently changed to a later date or evening time. Its separate 6 November page heading also remains intact.

## Part 1: military situation after the collapse in Transylvania

The 196-coordinate source is length-consistent. Raw text:

```text
OHLOPXXFEINDLAGEXVOELLIGEDEROUTEINSIEBENBUERGENUNDWAFFENSTILLSTANDUNGARNSMACHTMILITA?RISCHELAGEDER
```

Filling its one printed dash, source 21→A, gives:

```text

```

The fragment addresses OHL/OP and says that the complete collapse in Transylvania and Hungary's armistice affect the military situation. It stops at `DER`; the absent following wording is not supplied.

## Part 4: secure Kronstadt and Hermannstadt, then move material

The page advertises 264 coordinates but prints 258 literal slots. The first row's second group is the four-character `AAAV`. Two other literal glyphs are outside the coordinate alphabet: N at source 115 and C at source 216. They occupy printed slots and are treated separately from unprinted coordinates.

Under the primary conditional geometry, the raw 132-position reading is:

```text
OXKXM0HATMASSNAHMENZURSICHERUNGVONKRONST?D1UNDHERMANNSTADTGETROFFENUNDB?AB?ICHTIGTM?TABTRAN?PORTVONM?TE?IALI?N9ONMORGENABZUBEGINNENX
```

The explicit candidate is:

```text
OXKXMXHATMASSNAHMENZURSICHERUNGVONKRONSTADTUNDHERMANNSTADTGETROFFENUNDBEABSICHTIGTMITABTRANSPORTVONMATERIALIENVONMORGENABZUBEGINNENX
```

It reports measures to secure Kronstadt and Hermannstadt and an intention to begin transporting material the following day. It does not independently prove that transport subsequently occurred.

### Two missing units and every tied placement

The source deficit is modeled as **one coordinate in the short `AAAV` group plus a separate five-coordinate group**. The verifier checks every combination of the five candidate boundaries 5–9 in the short group and all 259 boundaries for the five-coordinate loss: **1,295 models**.

For the declared candidate, the minimum is three changes to observed coordinates. The five-coordinate gap is at source boundary **69**, between the second and third printed rows. The single-coordinate insertion ties at **5, 6, 7 or 8**. Each inserts A into the existing run of As, making `AAAAV`; presentation uses index 8, before the V. All four source ownership maps and raw readings are retained, even though their completed ciphertext is identical. The five-coordinate fill is `GVGVA`.

The primary candidate changes source 19 A→X, 46 G→F and 100 X→G; fills printed N and C with V; and fills the six unprinted coordinates. These are exact reversible edits. The fit is conditional on the explicit candidate and the one-plus-five loss family; it is not an independent original-text witness.

### Darkened A/X-like glyph

Source 19, the first glyph of the first row's fifth group, is darkened and A/X-like. The primary transcript reads A; a separate enlarged crop and **X alternative** are retained. Under X, the candidate needs two observed-coordinate changes instead of three. A complete second 1,295-model screen preserves the same four tied minima. The primary totals use A, so the favorable alternative is not silently substituted to reduce the repair count.

## Part 5: explicit interference, a conditional partial reading

The source advertises 252 coordinates. It contains **215 literal slots**, including **four printed dashes**, and two explicit `INTERFERENCE` annotations at source boundaries 190 and 215. Therefore, if the advertised length is accepted, the two unprinted runs total **37 coordinates**. The four dashes are already occupied source slots and are not added to that deficit.

The verifier retains **all 38 nonnegative allocations**, from 0/37 through 37/0. There is no automatic equal split or assignment based on the width of the printed annotation. Across all 38 models, 64 plaintext positions have the same singleton value; the complete union of possible domains is preserved.

The optional 20-character lexical crib `ANSCHLIESSENDMUESSEN`, at position zero, is compatible with all observed coordinates only for allocation **0/37**. Every other allocation needs at least one observed-coordinate contradiction in that crib. This is a **conditional choice**: it assumes that the prefix is the intended wording and was copied correctly at its observed coordinates. It does not prove that the first interference interval had zero lost symbols. The first marker can describe reception trouble without a net missing coordinate only under this model; all other allocations remain available.

Raw under 0/37:

```text
ANS?HLI?SSE?DMUE?SEN?ORB?GNN?MI?I?AER?SC??RSO?RG?N?ENP?RS??ALD?RW?R?SSH?FT??UNQ?ER?K?TUN?SS??EBE?B6?N?VEM?ER??GES?HO?E?WER?EN?
```

Only four independently declared word spans are completed: `ANSCHLIESSENDMUESSEN`, `MILITAERISCHER`, `PERSONALDER`, and `NOVEMBERABGESCHOBENWERDEN`. Every observed coordinate agrees with those spans. The resulting partial candidate is:

```text
ANSCHLIESSENDMUESSEN?ORB?GNN?MILITAERISCHERSO?RG?N?ENPERSONALDERW?R?SSH?FT??UNQ?ER?K?TUN?SS??EBE?B6?NOVEMBERABGESCHOBENWERDEN?
```

This fills three of the four printed dashes and eighteen of the 37 unprinted coordinates, with **zero observed-coordinate substitutions**. It increases fixed positions from 85 to 106 under the selected geometry; twenty plaintext positions remain unresolved. The awkward observed letters, including the middle of the sentence, are retained. A smooth complete sentence, military event, date interpretation or missing numerical value is not imposed. The surviving/compatible words indicate a discussion of personnel and removal in November, without recovering the full governing conditions.

## Part 6: unread contextual fragment

The source prints no RICHI length. It has a leading `INTERFERENCE` annotation, followed by 74 literal slots, including three dashes. The verifier records all **214 even total lengths from 74 through 500**, with the difference treated as unknown leading coordinates. Length 74 is included only as a zero-loss diagnostic endpoint.

No total length is selected and no readable body is asserted. The finite range is a bounded investigation, not an upper bound on the historical transmission. This fragment lives in `contextual_unread_records`; it is excluded from all five-record restoration totals and the catalog proposal.

## Part 7: a request involving the general political situation

The 248-coordinate source fits its advertised length:

```text
ALLGEMEINERHIERNICHTBEKANNTERPOLITISCHERLAGEXXEVTLXEINTRITTEINESWAFFENS?ILLSTANDESVXABHAENGIGZUMACHENWAEREXDRINGENDERBETENXX
```

Filling the printed dash at source 227 with X gives `WAFFENSTILLSTANDES`; no observed coordinate changes. The fragment refers to the general political situation, unknown to the sender, and the possible occurrence of an armistice. Its governing wording lies in absent/unread material, so the edition does not supply a complete policy instruction. Raw `VX` before `ABHAENGIG` remains unchanged.

## Part 8: acknowledge receipt

The 140 printed coordinates give:

```text
GLENCHESDURCHFER4SPRUCHVEMPFANGBESTAETIGENXXOXKXMX1ANOX11226O6XGEHEIMX
```

Three observed-coordinate substitutions—source 9 V→X, 34 G→D, and 124 X→V—give:

```text
GLEICHESDURCHFERNSPRUCHXEMPFANGBESTAETIGENXXOXKXMX1ANOX11226O6XGEHEIMX
```

These repair `GLEICHES`, `FERNSPRUCH` and the separator before `EMPFANG`. The complete reference `1ANOX11226O6XGEHEIMX` is unchanged, including the letter O in the apparent number. No normalization of I/1 or O/0 is made.

## Bounded copy search and remaining gaps

All six surviving physical sources, including the unread part 6, are searched against all **788** archived OCR blocks. The method compares exact ten-coordinate ADFGVX windows within each contiguous printed span, excludes only the listed self-blocks, and never crosses an `INTERFERENCE` annotation or invalid glyph. All hits are retained.

The only nonself result is three overlapping windows, a twelve-coordinate stretch, between part 8 and `p146_ocr_block4`. This short match is not certified as a duplicate and supplies no missing part. The other five queries have no nonself exact ten-coordinate match in this bounded corpus. This does not exclude a corrupted, differently keyed, differently divided or untranscribed copy. Parts 2 and 3 remain unlocated; they cannot be directly queried without an independent fragment.
